canonicalization.profile: JSON with object keys sorted (code-unit order), no whitespace, scalars as JSON.stringify would emit them, undefined omitted, integers only; hash = sha256 over the UTF-8 bytes
canonicalization.note: conditional keys are present only when the record carried them; absent keys are absent from the bytes, not null

merkle.rule: node = sha256(left_hex + right_hex) over the hex strings; an odd node is promoted unhashed; the leaf is the record hash

seal.rule: sealHash = sha256(canonical({v, agentId, plate, sealSeq, windowStart, windowEnd, count, issuedCount, seqStart, seqEnd, merkleRoot, deskCondition, prevSealHash[, rvnBlock][, profileHash]}))

root.rule: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s verify(publicKeyRaw, canonical(statement) bytes, signature); statement.keys are the keys this registry signs with

registrySignature.rule: HYBRID: for each entry in signatures, verify(keys[alg,keyId].publicKeyRaw, sealHash bytes, signature) — Ed25519 for alg ed25519, ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) for alg ml-dsa-65; ALL must verify. keyId = sha256(SPKI or raw key)[:16]. root, when present, is the SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s statement of these keys.

binding.rule: registry signature(s) over canonical(fields): each of `signatures` with the registrySignature.keys entry of the same alg/keyId (hybrid: all must verify); `signature` is the Ed25519 half

rules: assertion: WebAuthn signature = ECDSA-P256/SHA-256 over authenticatorData || sha256(clientDataJSON), verified with publicKey.raw (uncompressed point); clientDataJSON.type must be "webauthn.get"; authenticatorData flags must include UV (user verified)

binding: verify each of binding.signatures (or binding.signature with alg ed25519) over canonical(binding.fields) with the matching registrySignature.keys entry — Ed25519 and, when present, ML-DSA-65; all must verify; binding.fields.recordHash must equal recordHash, binding.fields.credentialId must equal the assertion credential, and binding.fields.publicKey must equal approver.publicKey.raw (17 Oct 2026: an assertion re-signed by another key, with that key offered, passes every other check)

identity: when binding.fields.identityProvider is present (18 Oct 2026), approver.identity must equal {provider: fields.identityProvider, tenantId: fields.tenantId, subjectId: fields.subjectId}: the tenant that vouched for the approver is inside the registry-signed binding, and the readable copy beside it may not differ

challenge: when approver.challenge is present (rule ask-v1, ceremonies from 18 Oct 2026), clientDataJSON.challenge must equal base64url(sha256(canonical(challenge.fields))) with fields.attestationId = approver.attestationId AND = record.attestationId AND = binding.fields.attestationId (19 Oct 2026: the sealed record and the signed binding name the ceremony; approver.attestationId alone is unsigned, and a genuine answer to another ask by the same credential would otherwise pass beside the binding of this record), fields.prompt = decision.prompt and fields.actionParamsHash = decision.actionParamsHash: the device signed over the ask, so the assertion itself names the act it answered. Absent, the challenge was a nonce and only the binding pairs the assertion with the record (an assertion by the same credential over another ask passes every other check)

amendment: when decision.amendment.command is present (approved WITH CHANGES), record.paramsHash must equal sha256(canonical(amendment.boundAs)) and amendment.boundAs.command must equal the amended command (its first 2000 UTF-16 code units): the SEALED record commits to the amended command; boundAs is the exact action binding the registry hashed ({tool, command, path, summary, amount, artifactHash}), served because record.tool and record.summary are capped, trimmed copies. A record with no paramsHash (ceremonies sealed before 19 Sep 2026) commits to no command: the amendment is then readable text, not checkable, and never confirmed. A bundle without boundAs (served before 19 Oct 2026) is checked with {tool: record.tool, command, path: null, summary: record.summary, amount: null, artifactHash: null}, exact only for a summary under the 400-char cap: download it again. When decision.actionParamsHash is present, amendment.originalParamsHash must equal it (the amendment cites the ask the person signed); an escalated approver's ask before 19 Oct 2026 carries no action digest and the citation is then not checkable. The passkey covers the ask as proposed; the amendment rests on the registry seal, not on a signature by the person (19 Oct 2026)

decision.attestationHashRule: sha256 over the registry's canonical attestation JSON (utils/attestationHashUtils.computeAttestationHash: id, prompt, response, status, respondedAt, approver, method, amendment, delivery, chain …); recomputable on the registry, cited here so the record and this decision are bound

anchor.rule: proof.txHex is the raw anchor transaction: its OP_RETURN payload is "xCk" + version + flags + 4 id bytes + hash(32), where hash is sealHash, or — when anchor.manifest is present — the manifest root that anchor.manifest.path reaches from sealHash (side L: sha256(sibling + current); side R: sha256(current + sibling)); sha256d(txHex) reversed = proof.txid; sha256d(headerHex) reversed = proof.blockHash; proof.merkleBlockHex is a Bitcoin-style merkleblock whose partial Merkle tree reproduces the header Merkle root and includes txid. The one outside fact left: that blockHash is on the Ravencoin chain.

howToVerify: 1. canonicalize `record` per `canonicalization.profile`, sha256 it, compare to `recordHash`
2. walk `merkle.proof` from `recordHash` (L: sha256(step+cur), R: sha256(cur+step)); the result must equal `seal.merkleRoot`
3. canonicalize the seal fields per `seal.rule`, sha256 it, compare to `seal.sealHash`

4. verify every entry of `registrySignature.signatures` over the seal hash with the key of the same alg/keyId in `registrySignature.keys` (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 when hybrid); older bundles: Ed25519-verify `signature` with `publicKeyRaw`

5. if `approver` is present: verify the WebAuthn assertion with `approver.publicKey.raw`, then Ed25519-verify `approver.binding.signature` over canonical(`approver.binding.fields`) with the registry key, and require `approver.binding.fields.publicKey` to equal `approver.publicKey.raw`: the binding, not the bundle, names the key the assertion may be checked with; when `approver.challenge` is present, recompute base64url(sha256(canonical(`challenge.fields`))) and require it to equal `clientDataJSON.challenge`, with the fields equal to `approver.attestationId`, which must also equal `record.attestationId` and `binding.fields.attestationId`, `decision.prompt` and `decision.actionParamsHash`

6. if `anchor.proof` is present: check the OP_RETURN (the seal hash, or the manifest root that `anchor.manifest.path` reaches from the seal hash), the txid, the header hash and the merkleblock; else look up `anchor.rvnTxId` on any Ravencoin explorer

8. if `seal.profileHash` is present: `profile.document` must be present, sha256(canonical(document)) must equal it, and `profile.signature` must verify over the hash with the registry keys; absent profileHash = sealed before profiles

7. if `basis`/`decision` are present: `basis.asked.recordHash` is another record on the same chain (fetch its bundle and run steps 1–4); `decision.attestationHash` equals `record.attestationHash`; when `decision.amendment.command` is present (approved WITH CHANGES), `record.paramsHash` must equal sha256(canonical(`amendment.boundAs`)) with `boundAs.command` equal to the amended command, and, when `decision.actionParamsHash` is present, `amendment.originalParamsHash` must equal it (approver.rules has the detail): the sealed record, not the readable amendment text, says what ran; the passkey covers the ask as proposed and the amendment rests on the registry seal

profile.rule: sha256(canonical(document)) = seal.profileHash; verify signature over the UTF-8 bytes of profileHash with the same registrySignature.keys as the seal; document.dials are the rules this node ran under when it sealed the window
